reason: A 2020 review of candidemia in Colombia cannot be the source for 2021 Mexican neonatal incidence, species share or the odds ratios given.
Excerpts cover EPA/DHA modulating CVD risk factors including inflammation but never mention eicosanoids or prostanoids, which may be covered in the mechanisms section not shown.
The 59% figure refers to all participants including the MICT group, not only HIIT completers; the design and non-significant MVPA change match.
Paper shows lung cancer as the leading cancer death only among Alaska Native people and US whites, not worldwide.
Paper finds histotype independently affects thymoma recurrence but not survival and does not address MG prognosis, so 'closely related to prognosis' overstates it.
The review covers adverse health effects of mercury in wildlife and humans, which supports a general background citation for toxic impacts in biota.
Paper supports arterial injury near genicular arteries during portal creation, but reports the popliteal artery (46%) as most often affected, not genicular arteries.
Paper uses Kalman filtering to assimilate animal-borne sensor data with location error into ocean-state estimates, not to filter animal movement paths as such.
Paper says MSK conditions are the most common pain complaints in primary care, not the most common organ system consulted for.
Crack-stopping by the polymer network is supported, but the Young's modulus and flexural strength values sit in a table whose numbers are not shown.
Cited as a prior report of EUS-guided needle sampling of cardiac masses, which this two-case EUS-FNA report supports; the FNB/ProCore details belong to the citing authors' own case.
The cited paper covers early Wuhan transmission dynamics and gives no estimate of asymptomatic prevalence, let alone rates up to 30.8%.
The paper studied carriers of several LRRK2 mutations and notes prior reports of dopaminergic deficits, but its own unaffected carriers had FDOPA uptake comparable to controls.
The paper supports ERRs in mitochondrial biogenesis but concludes that muscle ERRgamma activation failed to mitigate obesity and diabetes, contradicting the therapeutic-promise claim.
The protocol states that evidence shows antimicrobial properties of many herbs and that Chinese herbal medicine has been reported to have a therapeutic effect on SIBO.
The paper shows SIRT1 is needed for HIF-1alpha accumulation under hypoxia, but nothing shown establishes a proportional relationship.

The review links alpha to attention, but the target-area desynchronization wording comes from an alternative interpretation it tests, while its main thesis is alpha as active suppression of distracters.
The paper only restates earlier studies linking K. oxytoca outbreaks to sink drains, and its own outbreak was explicitly not drain-derived.
The burden-of-disease analysis ties rising case counts to population aging but says nothing about nDNA damage, oxidative damage or inflammation, which is the claimed mechanism.
The paper says advance care planning broadly, not advance directive completion specifically, is associated with higher satisfaction, and it does not say 'consistently'.
The cited paper is a SANS study of mixed micelles in bulk solution and does not address short-chain molecules immersing into the subphase of an interfacial monolayer.
Within a long multi-citation list, this paper supports the part it plausibly covers: smoking as a source of social belonging, smoker identity and group status.
Comparison and composite endpoint match, but the margin is a hazard ratio of 1.66, not 1.66%.

Ketosteroids gave weaker performance than cholesterol, but only cholest-4-en-3-one clearly cut lifespan and fecundity and the authors say they are not acutely toxic, so the claim is overstated for cholestan-3-one.
Paper links post-cardiac-surgery AKI to higher mortality and morbidity but does not address long-term survival.
Paper supports poor management among young adults but reports stable hypertension prevalence, not a rising trend in younger adults.
Review says chronic inflammatory signalling can contribute to cancer; the claim that most cancers are attributable to it is overstated.
Paper studies beta-globin cDNA transcripts and reports they are retained/degraded in the nucleus, matching the hedged use as partial prior evidence.
Paper states poverty hinders WASH practice, the point it plausibly supports among the co-cited works.
Review supports branched N-glycans on IGFR boosting signaling and tumour growth via galectin lattices, but not adhesion destabilization, IGFLR1 or AKT details.
Paper supports increased between-network connectivity and decreased DMN integrity, but found reduced within-network sensory connectivity and no frontoparietal change.
Cited paper is a GRU/CNN ensemble for DNA enhancer identification, not a stock-prediction RNN-CNN model the citing model could be compared against.
Paper notes Cdk1 phosphorylates regulators of nuclear-envelope breakdown but shows nothing on lamin A Ser22 or PKC.
Paper's own PD-1 monotherapy arm had zero responses; the 17% figure it reports belongs to another trial, so crediting it for a 5-20% ORR overstates its own finding.
Review supports growing use of high-resolution skin ultrasound but excerpts show nothing about SLEB being an increasingly frequent measured parameter.
CRISPR-Cas9 glycoengineering is correctly attributed, but the paper found glycans had only minor effect on ACE2 binding, so the steric-masking-of-binding point is overstated.
Paper supports annexin V binding PS on the inner leaflet but is a membrane-repair biophysics study and does not support the Annexin V-FITC necrotic-staining framing.
Paper reports maternal employment and lack of breastfeeding/infant-feeding counseling as significant factors, matching the points cited to it.
CaO2 as Ca2+ and H2O2 donor for ion interference is supported, but the paper shows no mitochondrial targeting.
The marked citation supports the cassava RAV melatonin/disease-resistance claim, which this sesame WRKY family survey does not address.
Paper shows combinations of policy and programme factors raising coverage, not mandatory vaccination policies or ESRD patients specifically.
The paper does use a hierarchical classification of cardiovascular discharge diagnoses, which is what the citation credits it for.
Review supports HDACs as epigenetic repressors of metabolic regulators and covers class-specific roles including vascular complications.
Cited case series describes COVID-19 clinical characteristics with no allergic-disease data, so it cannot be one of the contradictory observational findings.
The cited paper studies wear of coatings under refrigerant lubrication, not starved lubrication effects on film thickness or temperature.
The paper tests an education booklet intervention with no effect and links high education level to low incidence, not a positive education-IPV relationship.
Among several citations, this review plausibly supports the general need to evaluate training/implementation strategies in primary care, whose effectiveness it finds unclear.
GSK-3beta effects on ALP and cell-cycle proteins are supported, but the paper reports PER2 knockdown did not change osteogenic differentiation, only adipogenesis.
The paper only notes as a limitation that varied age, environment and health could not be controlled; it does not show confounders obscuring pollutant relationships or address TSH.
The paper reports DWV in Nayarit and the Federal District, but it did measure prevalence and loads, contrary to the qualifier.
The review attributes e-learning benefits to flexibility and access regardless of timescale, which supports learning at one's convenience.
The paper describes BMB2 as distantly related to TGB2 and includes HGSV in its alignment of the conserved central region between the two transmembrane domains.
The crisis-driven refocus on primary care is supported, but the excerpts do not show the 2017 opening of 200+ units or the ESF co-funding.
The paper used StringTie v2.1.4 on RNA-seq data but is not the tool's source and used it for transcript assembly, not FPKM expression.
The paper reports high prevalence in a rural/suburban patient group but does not test rural residence, crowding or water source as risk factors.
The case report covers PEG-tube infection and biofilm, but the excerpts never address contact with resident bacteria, microbiota or staff as the contamination route.
The review supports anodal tDCS improving cognition in the elderly, but it does not show it works better when combined with other interventions, and one combined study failed.
The marker sits on the IQR value 14 in the citing paper's own table, so it looks like a parsing artifact; the cited paper reports a different SAVR stay in another cohort.
SolexaQA is the package that includes DynamicTrim quality trimming with a user-set threshold; the cutoffs are the citing authors' own settings.
The interview study shows many unpublished implementations and little outcome data, but the excerpts do not address under-reporting or publication bias directly.
The cited paper gives FH prevalence between 1/500 and 1/200; the co-cited 1/250 falls inside that range.
The study used a similar sniff-and-rest timing and found subjective differences between fragrances, but it never tested the time span, and the physiological differences mostly vanished.
The guide describes Hill numbers in effective-number units, extended to phylogenetic diversity.
The review lists the same four nPKCs as Ca2+-independent and DAG-responsive, with roles in T cells; the 10-isoform count sits in a different, uncited sentence.
HemI is the tool cited for hierarchical clustering with a choice of linkage and distance options.
Loss of Dok2 sped up EGFR-driven lung tumors in mice but not Kras-driven ones, so the general claim leaves out that limit.
Paper reports grid cells as the most abundant hippocampus-projecting spatial cell type, the point this citation covers among several refs.
General oxidative-stress review mentions isoproterenol models but excerpts do not show the early-hours oxidative stress, inflammation or 24 h infarction timeline.
Paper calls alumina one of the most commonly used structural ceramics, supporting the general importance claim among several refs.
Review supports aneuploidy gain during azole selection and experimental evolution, but stresses it is mostly transient, so 'permanent' overstates it.
Paper supports restriction to sub-Saharan Africa, 36 countries and rural foci; the case numbers likely come from other refs in the range.
Paper links more comorbidities to worse mental-health HRQOL in older adults, not depression risk as such.
Excerpts name animal hosts but never describe animal-to-human transmission, which the review may cover elsewhere.
Paper states TNM staging, including lymph node status, is the basis of CRC therapy and guides treatment, supporting the background claim.
Review reports anxiety, depression and stress as common mental health responses to the pandemic, supporting the general claim alongside another ref.
Commentary reports large risk reductions from distancing and masks, supporting the effectiveness of the recommended control measures this ref covers.
Paper shows tumor irradiation enhancing adoptively transferred NK cell efficacy in vivo, but not RT-driven NK expansion or lymph node accumulation.
The paper studies arterial endothelial injury as an atherosclerosis-related model, a fair example for this broad background point.
The review covers these herbals for weight loss in mostly adult evidence, with energy-expenditure and reduced-absorption mechanisms.
The paper links Manaus's failed containment to the gamma variant spreading across Brazil; the two-thirds-of-deaths figure plausibly comes from co-cited ref 4.
The review supports fat-quality effects on lipids and insulin, but found no effect on fasting glucose, so 'glycemic levels' is overstated.
The paper supports genetic variation in individual radiation response, but for normal-tissue toxicity, not tumor response or tumor type.
The paper describes motion, eddy and fieldmap phase-unwrapping distortion correction, but not denoising, Gibbs ringing or bias-field steps.
The paper states renal recovery after obstruction depends partly on the presence of infection.
The study confirms PSQI covers the last 4 weeks but only applied it to ages 6 to 24; it does not establish general use for everyone over 6.
The paper supports harm from continuous PM exposure and notes effects depend on PM type and size; chemical composition is plausibly from co-cited ref 7.
The paper shows hMSC promote breast tumors in mice but shows no dose or combination comparison supporting the added-risk detail.
The paper is the group's THP1-based screening protocol, a reasonable method citation for parallel THP1 testing.
The paper infers unknown connections from time-series data, a related reconstruction task rather than link prediction of missing links in a partly known network.
Excerpts discuss allograft infection risks but never mention component migration or loosening, which may or may not appear elsewhere.
The paper supports only the extraction-solvent effect; plant part, harvest time and geoclimatic factors are not shown.
The cited meta-analysis used MetaQC/MetaDE with a fixed-effect model, not forest plots from the R package meta with subgroup and sensitivity analyses.
The paper shows preclinical anti-cancer activity and calls artemisinin a potential candidate, so saying it is used in cancer treatment with good efficacy overstates it.
The case report supports ultrasound of the vocal cords but describes use by anesthesiologists, not pulmonologists.
The review gives 1-5% incidence for all sternal wound infections and 10-30% mortality, not deep infections or up to 47%.
The paper names RT-qPCR as the lab-bound gold standard and is itself about RT-LAMP, so it does not show qPCR as a point-of-care tool.
Excerpts link self-regulation to goal monitoring and overcoming barriers but do not show the claim about setting more realistic and challenging goals.
The paper is a lab study of mouse, monkey and human saliva that drew some samples from a cohort, so calling it a cohort study misstates the design.
Windle et al. find no gold-standard resilience measure and make a strong case for developing valid measures that assess a range of resilience processes.
The MERS study shows a strong pro-inflammatory cytokine response and says inflammation may relate to severity, but it did not assess outcomes, so 'determine progression and mortality' overstates it.
The cited study concludes the AcrAB efflux pump contributes to ciprofloxacin resistance in K. pneumoniae, which is the point credited to it; the expression data are the citing authors' own.
The paper says early-adult ACE effects are understudied and most prior work used clinical or cross-sectional samples, but it is a US study and says nothing about low-middle-income settings.
The cited paper compares Padua and Caprini scores in general medical inpatients and finds both usable; it does not address lung cancer patients on immune checkpoint inhibitors.

The meta-analysis found a positive pooled effect over nonblended learning, but after publication-bias adjustment the effect was not significant and the authors conclude only 'more or at least as effective', so a definite increase overstates certainty.
The IRT tutorial states that separating item properties lets assessments be adapted while keeping a common reference, supporting the point this co-citation plausibly covers.
Excerpts show CNR and SlAP2a homologues differentially expressed and TAGL1 not, and the reported count of six DE genes fits the claim; nothing shown contradicts it.
The paper measured self-reported mental health problems in detained JSOs with the MAYSI-2, but the excerpts show no prevalence figures, which could be in unshown results.
The paper presents a PAL/TAL/HAL phylogeny but the excerpts never mention PAM, so whether the cladogram's PAL/PAM groups derive from it cannot be confirmed.
The paper calls costs 'a major driver' and says very low costs may lead to excessive or uncritical prescribing; 'main driver' and 'largely irrational' use overstate it.
The cited paper reports obesity prevalence and risk in COVID-19 inpatients and says nothing about weight stigma, the point this sentence credits to it.
The cited meta-analysis compares irradiated vs unirradiated and left vs right sides and presents no mean-heart-dose risk model.
The cited paper is a clinical MRgFUS blood-brain barrier opening study, fitting its listing as an included focused ultrasound article.
The review links polar auxin transport to adventitious root formation in trees, not PIN-mediated lateral root differentiation.
The review describes the mutation-based neoantigen prediction pipeline using MHC binding and gene expression; file-specific details plausibly come from the co-cited work.
The cited study tests NLR as a predictor of mortality in patients already septic, not as a predictor of bacterial infection.
About 12 million new vehicles over seven years (about 1.7 million a year) supports the stated annual growth of about 1.5 million.
The cited review covers zebrafish models of metabolic disease, not metabolic rate or cardiac function in developmental or climate studies.
The review supports personalised management, but says GLP-1 receptor agonists slow gastric emptying rather than improve it.
The paper describes BWA and its BWA-SW algorithm, not the BWA-MEM algorithm named in the text.
The review gives TE classes summing to about 46% of the human genome and divides them into retrotransposons and DNA transposons.
The excerpts show a 0.5% working difference and the trade-off, but not the 0.2-0.8% range, which may be elsewhere in the paper.
The paper is an osteosarcoma metabolomics study, but of drug effects on lipid metabolism, not metabolic reprogramming in tumor progression.
Excerpts confirm no major adverse events but never say whether any patients had compensated cirrhosis; that may be in parts not shown.
The paper reports late tripolar mitoses only occasionally and used time-lapse plus single-cell genotyping, not fixed-embryo analysis; it cites others for fixed-embryo work.
The paper finds minimal added value from spectral bands while noting promising results elsewhere, so it fits as one side of discrepant findings.
As one of a range citation, the review supports altered BCAA/BCAT1 metabolism driving progression and poor outcomes, the oncogenic-gain point.
It is a primary-care study of national dementia diagnosis rates, but nothing shown concerns BAME groups; the population detail is wrong.
The paper compares tumor clonal evolution trees, loosely related to disease evolutionary histories, but not ancestral genome reconstruction or the listed applications.
FPG cost/availability and A1C advantages are supported, but the paper says A1C needs no fasting, the reverse of 'need fasting samples'.
The study shows CD40-licensed cDC1 are required for optimal anti-tumour immunity, supporting it as one of several studies on activated cDC roles.
The paper states germline APC mutation causes FAP and APC loss promotes beta-catenin/TCF4 transcription in colorectal tumourigenesis.
The paper notes heavy-metal pollution has been found to affect condition and health of nestlings, supporting the general background claim.

Paper reports IL-20 induces TNF-a, IL-1b, MMP-1 and MMP-13 in OASFs and raises IL-6/MMPs while lowering TGF-b, BMP-2 and aggrecan in chondrocytes, and lists the named disease roles; 'secretion' is loose wording for measured expression.
Review on natural variation in photosynthesis frames it as a way to study plant-environment interactions, enough for this general background point shared with another citation.
Paper supports parental safety and environment-quality perceptions as barriers to outdoor play, but nothing shown covers socioeconomic inequality or uneven green-space distribution.
Manzi et al. used a white-plate-calibrated colorimeter and CIELAB, but a handheld Minolta on liquid milk, not an UltraScan PRO with powder in a bag.
Cited editorial is about NK cells and belimumab response in pSS and gives no prevalence figure or ranking among autoimmune diseases.
Abstract lists strengthening governance and leadership among the key emerging ingredients for health sector reform, with focus on low-income settings.
Excerpts link North Atlantic cooling to southern European aridity in the Last Interglacial but do not show summer polar outbreaks, Mediterranean summer SST drops or thermocline erosion.
Paper describes music therapy as low-risk and cost-effective versus drugs with adverse effects, and shows growing research interest.

Paper paired soil phenolic acid measurements with rhizome transcriptomics to characterize differential phenolic acid metabolism in continuous-cropping soil; metabolomic profiling is credited to other citations.
Included COVID-19 survivor cohort used Italian normative scores and an Italian team, consistent with listing it as an Italian study.
Sampling rate of 500 Hz matches, but the paper used a 32-channel NuAmp setup, not 22 channels.
The excerpts confirm PCR detection of G. duodenalis assemblages A and E in Bactrian camels, but the specific sample size and prevalence for camels are omitted from the provided text.

The cited paper introduces a database of microbial natural product structures and does not discuss marine algicolous fungi or their potential as sources of antifungal or insecticidal agricultural chemicals.

The cited paper explicitly notes that regular HIV-1 evolution (e.g., RT-mediated) cannot be formally excluded from contributing to escape, pointing to a substitution identified in the PAM region away from the Cas9 cleavage site.
The cited meta-analysis evaluated VEGF as a predictor of survival and prognosis in treated HCC, rather than for evaluating treatment efficacy directly.

The median survival numbers (22.0 and 13.0 months) are reported accurately, but they apply to the entire cohort of surgically treated patients (stages 0–IV), not exclusively to patients with advanced disease, although the abstract notes the majority presented with advanced stage.
The cited study evaluates P-wave and QT-interval dispersion in slow coronary flow and does not investigate or report on fragmented QRS complexes.

The excerpts discuss verifying normality and expressing differences as percentages when variability increases with magnitude, but cut off mid-sentence when discussing what to do if differences are not normally distributed.

The cited paper contradicts the claim, stating that Ti-6Al-4V (Grade V) has a Young's modulus of 105–120 GPa and that conventional titanium alloys suffer from stress shielding caused by a mismatched elastic modulus, unlike newer alloys developed to match bone (40–60 GPa).
The cited paper introduces DESeq2 as a tool for differential expression analysis of RNA-seq count data, directly supporting its cited use.
The cited paper confirms that Med-PaLM was developed by applying parameter-efficient instruction prompt tuning to the Flan-PaLM model.
The cited study assessed anthropometric and body fat trajectories (BMI, fat mass index, weight, waist circumference) rather than the modulation of biological pathways.
The paper found snow gave inconsistent, short-term protection compared with leaf litter, consistent with low snow not lowering later abundance.
The paper describes PDR as stride-wise position updates that drift, not continuous velocity estimation giving a stable position, though PDR does derive position.
Shown haplotype figures (CVIET 71%) do not give the 83% value or name the exact mutation, which may appear in unshown results.
The paper supports nanotechnology's promise in cancer medicine only, not the broad claims about information, chemical industry or market potential.
The paper shows stress-related gene changes in amygdala and blood, but did not study the hippocampus.
The paper studies SAMC antitumor effects in breast cancer cells and says nothing about SAC conversion into SAMC or S-methyl cysteine in aged garlic.
The paper links endosomal TLRs, especially Tlr8, to SLE in mice but does not show high TLR7/8/9 expression in the listed diseases.
The paper describes high-fidelity simulation cases built to assess EPA 10 and entrustment, supporting its share of the multi-cited sentence.
The paper anticipates home monitoring and earlier detection of deterioration but says nothing about AI or shorter hospital stays.
The review covers lactate and LDH in cancer metabolism, not LDH release as a marker of membrane damage and cell injury.
The review states pretreatments dissolve or remove hemicellulose, supporting the hemicellulose explanation this citation plausibly covers.
Cited paper used cell-SELEX against intact cells, consistent with selecting aptamers against an undisrupted whole target.
Excerpts confirm AlGaInP red emitters but show no wavelength range, which may appear elsewhere in the paper.
Cited paper reports only limited Siglec binding to sialylated HMOs and says sialic acid alone is not sufficient, so 'bind mainly' overstates it.
Cited randomized phase II trial reports afatinib activity and response comparable to cetuximab; survival detail is not contradicted.
